q: I have a job where I stand long hours every day and my body’s been especially taking a beating this week from it. I asked for a back massage- his response? My back hurts too from the gym.
cx: 15 weeks with her first, too tired after a standing job to keep up the house.

q: When I’m too tired to cook he never offers to cook. Before pregnancy I loved cooking so I always just did it. Now when Im just too tired after work we either just order or eat cereal/ something easy.
cx: She carried the cooking before pregnancy; her husband has not picked it up.

q: I wasn’t a coffee person before but still had energy to do everything. Now I am just gaining more weight and even to talk to a friend or family on phone, I literally have no energy.
cx: Four days from the third trimester and more tired each day.

q: I used to be terrified of birth now I just want it to come and relinquish me of my big belly prison.
cx: 34 weeks; discomfort has replaced her fear of birth.

q: He’ll help if I specifically ask him to, but I hate feeling like I have to manage another adult. I don’t want to assign every single task, remind him what needs to be done, or explain why maybe the overflowing laundry basket or dirty kitchen should be handled without me saying something.
cx: Eight weeks, nauseous and exhausted; she wonders if this is what he'll be like as a father.

q: This is my first pregnancy and I’ve been so careful about everything like sushi, cold cuts, etc… I’m so mad at myself for this and terrified to tell my husband what I think is going on.
cx: At 1:30am at 18 weeks, after eating a lot of raw cookie dough.

q: I recently went to my midwife appointment and she explained how dangerous it is and it scared me.
cx: A first-time mother told by her midwife never to kiss the baby because of cold sores.
r: medical condition (cold sores / virus risk to newborn)

q: I am 33w pregnant today, and have been having business trips (round trip 4 hours) the past 2 months staying over night at hotel every night except for Thursday and Friday night and the weekend. I miss my husband, my pets, and I feel grossed about myself and super bloated because I have to eat all my meals from outside being away from home. And gosh I miss my pregnancy pillow
cx: Client work at 33 weeks keeps her in hotels four nights a week.

q: I am telling myself that Imma be a mom so I better be strong and think positively but I can’t think straight today.
cx: After a night of three hours' sleep before another client day.

q: I have been belittled and made to feel embarrassed for reaching out with any concerns about my pregnancy to the point I don’t even want to walk into their office anymore. I feel like I’m “that patient” everyone dreads to see.
cx: At 36 weeks she asks about switching OBs.

q: I was lucky to have an "easy" and high energy pregnancy, even the first trimester. Then I got to about 33 weeks and just CRASHED.
cx: Outside the US/UK, in a country she calls 'pretty meh' for medical care.

q: I’m around machines that run hot and make you sweat your butt off on a cold winter day, and with this summer being as hot as it’s been, I’m miserable in there. We have to wear thick uniforms that is super unbreathable for sanitation so I don’t have the option of dressing down.
cx: 22 weeks, a packaging-plant supervisor on 9-11 hour days.

q: It’s very rare that I work 8 hours, I’m pretty much always there for 9-11 hours a day. The only time I get to sit down is my 30 minute break, other than that I’m on my feet all day long.
cx: Supervisor who starts an hour before her team.

q: I feel like my bosses are extremely inconsiderate to me being pregnant, my boss has never been pregnant
cx: Pressured back after one sick day; she once helped pregnant co-workers herself.

q: I feel trapped at my job as it’s the only thing close to my home and I never went to college so my options are very limited.
cx: Why she can't leave the packaging job.

q: Now that plan turned out differently because I was too tired even to lift my feet high enough in the first trimester, so I quit running for three months 😂
cx: A runner at 16 weeks whose plan to run all pregnancy broke in the first trimester.

q: My biggest concern is not overdoing it. I don't mind slowing down or even walking if needed, but I'm wondering: **how do you know you're pushing too hard?**
cx: Friends at her level are training for races or ran to the end.

q: I am so scared of tearing or needing an emergency C section that I feel a planned C section would be better bet.
cx: 38, first baby, 32 weeks, deciding on birth mode.

q: At latest antenatal class I freaked out and started crying when they started talking about recovery and breastfeeding while in pain.
cx: The antenatal class moment that pushed her to post.

q: My mother, MIL, most of my friends also had C sections and so I can’t talk to them about this.
cx: She has no one near her who has had a vaginal birth to ask.

q: the idea of not having a job to go back to and having to look for one as a new mom gives me lot of anxiety. I feel without having anything to go back to I will get lost in motherhood
cx: Made redundant days after her positive test.

q: It’s ultimately painful either way and women are expected to be up and taking care of babies so soon after birth.
cx: Agreeing with a reply that both birth routes are hard.

q: one question about peri bottle, is it necessary if you live in country which uses jet spray ?
cx: US recovery-kit advice doesn't fit her country's bathrooms.

q: he said it’s because I need to sleep 4-5 hours continuously a day and don’t (what new mother does daily without a nanny…).
cx: Five weeks after the birth, her doctor's answer to a recovery problem.
